query:
Sample: as-built laser powder bed fusion (LPBF) AlSi10Mg (no heat treatment known), mounted in phenolic, prepared by belt sanding, SiC papers P320 to P1200, 1 um alumina suspension on a napped pad (about 12 min), then 0.1 um water-based polycrystalline diamond suspension on a vibratory polisher (Buehler VibroMet 2, medium-nap synthetic cloth, 1-2 h), then ultrasonic cleaning in DI water and ethanol. No colloidal silica was used. Imaged at 5 kV in an Apreo SEM with both the Everhart-Thornley detector and a dedicated BSE detector; both detectors show the same contrast:
- angular, flat-topped particles 0.3-1.5 um across (median equivalent diameter 0.43 um), BRIGHTER than the Al matrix; about one per 26 um^2 (about 0.9% area fraction); some sit in small pockets with a dark rim;
- at 35,000x, a continuous network brighter than the cell interiors, spacing 0.5-0.8 um, all aligned in one direction across an 11.8 um field;
- dark spots 0.06-0.35 um (median 0.09 um), about 1.8 per um^2, darker than the matrix.
Questions:
(1) What are the bright particles most likely to be? Evaluate each candidate: eutectic or coarsened Si particles (including the coarse zones at melt-pool boundaries), Fe- and Mn-rich intermetallics (beta-Al5FeSi, alpha-Al(Fe,Mn)Si, pi-Al8FeMg3Si6), Mg2Si, oxides (Al2O3, MgO, MgAl2O4 spinel), embedded abrasives (alumina, SiC, diamond), and metallic debris (steel, zinc-plated steel, brass, saw-blade bond). For each, give the expected BSE contrast relative to the Al matrix and its EDS signature. Are sub-micron to micron Fe-rich intermetallic particles reported in as-built LPBF AlSi10Mg, at what size and number density, and do they appear bright in BSE? What Fe content is typical of LPBF AlSi10Mg powder, and does Fe partition to the cell boundaries?
(2) Is a bright cellular network in BSE consistent with the Si-rich eutectic cell boundaries of as-built LPBF AlSi10Mg, and what cell size is typical? How much could polishing relief from a 1-2 h napped-cloth diamond polish contribute?
(3) Given that the dark spots are dark in BSE as well, are they more consistent with embedded 0.1 um diamond, pores or pits, Mg2Si or oxides, or organic residue? Is diamond embedding in aluminum from fine diamond suspensions documented?
(4) What EDS conditions (beam energy, spot vs area, standards) can identify 0.3-1.5 um particles in an Al matrix, given the interaction volume at 5 kV and 15 kV?
Cite primary literature and manufacturer application notes, and say clearly where evidence is missing.
